jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
Cross Country is looking for top talent to join our team! We are a market-leading, tech-enabled workforce solutions and advisory firm with more than four decades of experience helping organizations solve complex labor and operational challenges. Recognized as a Top Place to Work by U.S. News & World Report and a Most Loved Workplace by Newsweek, Cross Country is committed to quality and excellence in everything we deliver. We were also the first public company to earn The Joint Commission Gold Seal of Approval® for Health Care Staffing Services Certification with Distinction — a standard we continue to uphold today.

BASIC PURPOSE

The Program Director is responsible for the strategic and operational leadership of the PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) center within the assigned region. This role ensures the delivery of high-quality, coordinated, and person-centered care that aligns with PACE regulatory requirements and organizational goals. The Program Director oversees program operations, drives year-over-year improvements, manages budgets and performance metrics, and ensures compliance with federal, state, and local regulations specific to the PACE model.

Essential Functions

Provide strategic leadership and operational oversight of the local Program Support Team, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and program objectives.
Develop and implement strategic plans for PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) program operations, including participant growth, service quality, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance.
Collaborate with executive leadership to align program goals with broader organizational strategy and community health needs.
Ensure alignment with PACE program model requirements by working closely with implementation and cross-functional internal teams.
Lead, mentor, and develop the Program Support Team, including ongoing coaching, performance management, and professional development.
Establish performance expectations and drive a culture of accountability, responsiveness, and high-quality service delivery.
Oversee daily operations of the program support team to ensure timely execution of deliverables, accuracy of documentation, and operational consistency.
Facilitate cross-functional communication to ensure coordinated, participant-centered care delivery across departments.
Drive participant satisfaction through high-quality care coordination, responsiveness, and effective communication.
Conduct regular participant and family visits to assess satisfaction, identify service gaps, and implement improvements.
Monitor and evaluate key performance indicators (KPIs), including participant satisfaction, health outcomes, service utilization, and operational efficiency to support continuous improvement.
Ensure full compliance with all CMS, state, and PACE-specific regulatory and licensing requirements.
Lead regular audits, quality reviews, and risk assessments; identify gaps and implement corrective action plans.
Maintain readiness for internal and external audits and ensure adherence to organizational and regulatory standards.
Build and maintain strong relationships with community providers, partner organizations, and regulatory agencies to support program growth and integration.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders to ensure effective care planning, coordination, and documentation.
Oversee program reporting, including preparation of performance reports, KPIs, and updates for executive leadership, board members, and regulatory agencies.
Serve as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders regarding program performance and initiatives.
Maintain awareness of industry trends, policy changes, and best practices in elder care and managed care delivery to support ongoing program improvement.
All other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

6+ years of experience in healthcare operations, program management, or related service delivery roles.
4+ years of leadership experience with operational oversight and full P&L responsibility.
Proven success managing complex healthcare programs and achieving financial, operational, and strategic goals.
Prior experience managing PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) program accounts or home care operations strongly preferred.
Experience working in start-up or turnaround environments strongly preferred.
Strong knowledge of healthcare service delivery models, compliance standards, and regulatory requirements.
Experience conducting client visits, satisfaction reviews, and service quality assessments.
Proven success in client relationship management, account growth, and cross-functional team leadership.
Strong collaboration skills with sales, operations, and account management teams to drive growth and service excellence.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, negotiation, and presentation skills.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
Ability to lead teams in fast-paced, high-accountability environments while maintaining operational quality and performance standards.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and comfort using virtual collaboration platforms such as Microsoft Teams and Zoom.
Familiarity with MSP/VMS technology systems preferred.

Education: High school diploma or equivalent required; Bachelor’s degree in business, healthcare or other similar discipline preferred or equivalent combination of education and experience to successfully perform the essential functions of the job.

Company equipment(laptop, monitor, keyboard, mouse headset) will be provided directly to you for use during employment.

Benefits

Cross Country offers a competitive compensation, benefits, and wellness program, including Medical Insurance, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Disability Insurance, Voluntary Insurance, 401(k) plan, Tuition Assistance, and Pet Insurance. The company offers a variety of Wellness options through Burnalong, which offers a robust online platform of classes and programs as well as local gym access.

Cross Country is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE) - Veteran/Disability

jobs.title: Landscape Architecture - Business Development Director
jobs.description:
Department:
Landscape Architecture
Location:
Oakland, CA
Compensation:
$140,000 - $180,000 / year

Description

Alta is looking for a Landscape Architecture/Urban Design Business Development Director
to join our growing Oakland office design team. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who believes in the power of design and placemaking to create vibrant, active communities, and engaging public spaces.

In this role, you will drive business development and strategic growth throughout the Bay Area, Northern California, and the Pacific Northwest,
establishing Alta's presence and reputation with local city and regional government clients. You will be responsible for leading client relationship building, identifying new opportunities, and positioning Alta as a leader in sustainable landscape design and active transportation. This role requires a strategic thinker who can expand our market share while maintaining the high-quality, collaborative approach that defines our work.

You will also work on the design of projects with a focus on sustainability and active communities around the West and across the country. Design professionals who enjoy working closely with other disciplines will appreciate our Oakland team's multi-disciplinary approach that encourages collaboration with our planners, engineers, graphics designers, outreach specialists, and data analysts. If you are looking to join an innovative organization and do work that connects people to places while advancing social justice, safety, and environmental resilience, apply with Alta today!

About Alta

Alta is a mission‑driven company working to mitigate climate change and advance safety and social justice by shaping sustainable, people‑centered communities. We bring together expertise across planning, design, engineering, education and encouragement programs, and community engagement to help communities thrive. Our work is grounded in the belief that how places are designed and experienced has a profound impact on equity, health, and opportunity—and that people should always be at the heart of those decisions.

Founded in 1996, Alta was at the forefront of the active transportation movement and has spent nearly 30 years partnering with communities to imagine a more connected, resilient, and inclusive future. Today, with more than 225 staff across the United States and beyond, we are a global leader in creating environments that support everyday life, strengthen human connection, and respond to the challenges of a changing world. Alta offers the opportunity to collaborate across disciplines, contribute to meaningful work at every scale, and be part of a team committed to making lasting, positive change for people and the places they call home.

Day to Day

Day-to-day responsibilities for this role would include:
Leading business development efforts throughout Northern California and the Pacific Northwest including identifying opportunities, cultivating client relationships with local city and regional government agencies, and developing winning proposals and presentations.
Driving strategic market growth and positioning Alta as a leader in sustainable landscape architecture, urban design, and active transportation within the region.
Contributing to revenue growth targets for the Landscape Architecture business line in Northern California and the Pacific Northwest.
Building and maintaining relationships with key decision-makers at public agencies, participating in industry events, and representing Alta in the professional community.
Providing leadership and technical expertise to the Oakland and Portland Landscape Architecture design teams. In addition, collaborate with other disciplines (planning, engineering, data) as needed.
Mentoring design staff and contributing to internal professional development and training to design team.
Implementing best practices and process improvements to enhance project delivery efficiency and effectiveness.
Workload balancing for the Oakland and Portland Design teams.
Preparing schedules, budgets, and scope of services for projects.
Providing quality control over team deliverables.

Qualifications

Required

This position requires a combination of skills, experience and education including, but not limited to
15+ years of experience as a Landscape Architect or Urban Designer in a consulting environment or public entity
Bachelor's degree in Landscape Architecture or Urban Design
Professional Landscape Architect (PLA)
Experience in, or knowledge of corridors, such as greenways, trails, streets, or canals.
Demonstrated understanding of the design process and working collaboratively with other design disciplines and a detailed understanding of project management principles, methods and techniques.
Business acumen and demonstrated experience in business development and managing large contracts.
Ability to guide staff members and manage internal team expectations.
Exhibits strong initiative and ability to capitalize on opportunities to enhance Alta's position in the marketplace.
Ability to manage competing priorities, multiple simultaneous projects involving cross-functional project teams within budgetary and schedule constraints.
Excellent professional ethics, leadership skills, accountability, and decision-making capabilities.
Good presentation skills.
Proficiency in an enterprise-wide resource planning and project management tool.
Ability and willingness to travel.

Preferred

There are a number of additional skills, experience, and education that would be beneficial to this position including, but not limited to:
Experience managing large projects for both private and public clients.
Experience working in urban, rural, suburban, land use contexts.
Experience using Deltek Vision.
Active participation in industry-relevant professional associations and committees, such as ASLA or ULI.

What We Offer

Flexible Schedule

Alta offers a flexible, hybrid work schedule where most employees work from home three days per week. In-office days support our collaborative culture, one of our core values.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is $140,000-$180,000. This range reflects the company’s good faith estimate of the compensation for this position at the time of posting. Final compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location.

Benefits

Alta offers comprehensive benefits to all full-time employees:
Medical
: PPO or HSA medical plans, Alta pays 75% of the cost
Dental/Vision
: PPO, Alta pays 90% of the cost
Life Insurance
: Alta pays 100% of the premium for life and AD&D, equal to your base compensation
401(k)
: Alta provides a match up to 3%
PTO
: 21 days accrued annually to start
Holidays
: 11 total company paid holidays
Paid Parental Leave/Short-Term Disability

Additional Benefits
: Wellness reimbursement up to $800 annually, Alta Gets Around benefit of up to $900 annually, 5-year travel award, and professional development opportunities

jobs.title: Client Development Director
jobs.description:
Job Summary

CLIENT DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR

Location
: Preference for candidate to be based in a major city on the West Coast such as Phoenix, Las Vegas, Salt Lake City, Denver, San Francisco, Seattle, etc.

Division
: Ticketmaster

Line Manager:
EVP, Head of Sports

Contract Terms:
Permanent, Full-Time, 40 hours per week

Who We Are

We’re fans who help fans everywhere get in to the live events they love. A proud division of Live Nation Entertainment, Ticketmaster has changed the way the world connects with their favorite artists, teams, and shows, and we continue to shape innovation every day. We’re not just selling tickets (though we do that better than anyone else), we’re enriching lives one amazing experience at a time. And we think that’s pretty amazing. If you’re passionate about the magic of live entertainment like we are, and you want to work at a company dedicated to helping millions of fans experience it, we want to hear from you.

THE TEAM

The Client Development team uses flexibility, creative thinking, organizational skills, and relationship building to work with our clients on our products, vision, and industry needs. This team of leaders, strategists and collaborators must always balance the unique best interests of our clients with Live Nation Entertainment’s vision and priorities. This team is client first and always ready to have the tough (and easy) conversations! We are part of the North American Client Development organization, working with Ticketmaster’s Global Marketplace organization, which sells over 500 million tickets each year across professional and college sports, theatre, arts, and concerts.

THE JOB

The Client Development Director (CDD) will focus exclusively on our client accounts, concentrating on the needs of clients within the TM Sports segment. This position will be responsible for managing, supporting and servicing the account related needs of any assigned set of clients in addition to sourcing and securing new business.

What You Will Be Doing

Operate as the voice of the customer internally by working with other Ticketmaster business leaders to provide incredible client experiences and outcomes
Direct and collaborate on the development of an account management blueprint, ensuring maximization of revenue and renewals within our client base.
Develop and implement strategies to upsell existing clients on products, programs, or services that drive ticket sales and revenue for your segment; track, monitor, and adjust plans to maximize results.
Develop, share, and implement best practices for assigned market segments.
Forecast clients’ tickets & revenue contribution to the segment’s annual business plan by developing client level business plans, including account strategy, profitability analysis, and program projections.
Complete ad hoc sales operations support as requested.
Monitor service levels provided by support teams to ensure SLA’s are being met.
Coach and collaborate with others on client support, marketing, and account management teams to ensure effective, consistent communication of Ticketmaster’s capabilities, services, and relevant offerings for our clients.
Responsible for retention of all clients within assigned portfolio, ensuring maximum margin levels through the renewal engagement.
Comprehensively collaborate with a cross-functional team, providing distinct support functions to clients, ultimately maximizing client satisfaction scores.
Identify new business opportunities, directing the client acquisition process against a set of annual sales goals.
Proactively conduct strategic account reviews with all assigned clients on a regular basis to review service needs and sales trends. Identify products and pricing that meet client needs and business objectives.
Development relationships with key system and product users providing product team with client feedback on product enhancements.
Assist in the identification of opportunities for new products and enhancements for development of existing products.
Address client concerns and ensure for the resolution of issues in a timely manner, with follow-up when appropriate.
Deliver ongoing market analysis and assessment of competitors and market intelligence with a focus on the future and value creation.
Maintain company’s contact management database (Salesforce) with accurate, up-to-date contact and account details.
Monitor and report on the activities of competitors and potential collaborators identifying new business opportunities and threats.
Coordinate responses of RFP’s.
Retain accounts through the development of strong relationships with key decision makers and users within an organization.
Responsible for TM1 Marketing product adoption and managing its local nuances.
35%-50% travel required

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW (or TECHNICAL SKILLS)

Minimum 10-12 years’ experience in the live entertainment industry with a strong focus on account management and account development
BA/BS or College diploma in Business, Marketing or related field and/or equivalent work-related experience.
Experience with live event ticketing or real-time inventory management systems preferred.
Strong presentation and project management skills.
Proven track record of exceeding sales targets.
Experience leading change in a complex matrix-oriented organization with strong emphasis on team development.
High level knowledge of digital media and industry trends.
Strong competence in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Experience in the live entertainment industry, especially with a major league sports team and major market venue is highly desirable.
AI skills and understanding highly desirable.
Strong understanding of technology-enable products, software platforms, APIs, integrations and data driven solutions for complex consultative sales cycles.
Experience creating and delivering client presentations

You (behavioral Skills)

Analytical and strategic thinking
Excellent customer service, communication, and consulting skills.

Benefits & Perks

Through our ‘Taking Care of Our Own’ program, we provide benefits across six key pillars:

HEALTH: Medical, vision, dental and mental health benefits for you and your family, with access to a health care concierge, and Flexible or Health Savings Accounts (FSA or HSA)
YOURSELF: Free concert tickets, generous paid time off including paid holidays, sick time, and personal days
WEALTH: 401(k) program with company match, stock reimbursement program
FAMILY: New parent programs including caregiver leave and baby bonuses, plus fertility, adoption, foster, or surrogacy support
CAREER: Career and skill development programs with School of Live, tuition reimbursement, and student loan repayment
OTHERS: Volunteer time off, crowdfunding match

LIFE AT TICKETMASTER

We are proud to be a part of Live Nation Entertainment, the world’s largest live entertainment company.

Our mission at Ticketmaster is to connect people around the world to the live events they love. Ticketmaster is the world’s largest ticket marketplace and the global market leader in live event ticketing products and services. Through official partnerships with thousands of venues, artists, sports teams, festivals, performing arts centers and theaters, Ticketmaster processes 550 million tickets per year across 35+ different countries.

We do it all with an intense passion for Live and an inspiring and diverse culture driven by accessible leaders, attentive managers, and enthusiastic teams. If you’re passionate about live entertainment like we are, and you want to work at a company dedicated to helping millions of fans experience it, we want to hear from you.

Our Work Is Guided By Our Values

Reliability
- Fans and clients count on us to power their live event experiences and we rely on each other to make it happen.

Teamwork
– While we celebrate individual achievements, we know have more success as a team.

Integrity
- We are committed to the highest moral and ethical standards on behalf of the countless partners and stakeholders we represent.

Belonging
- We are committed to building a culture in which all people can be their authentic selves, have an equal voice and opportunities to thrive.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Organization Overview

Founded in 1951 by Corning Incorporated as a gift to the nation, the Corning Museum of Glass (CMoG) is the global center for the art, science, and history of glass.

The Museum shapes the understanding and appreciation of glass worldwide and draws more than 300,000 visitors each year to a city of roughly 10,000 residents. The New York Times named CMoG as one of the U.S. museums to see in 2025, and Newsweek readers voted CMoG one of the Top 3 Best Art Museums in America.

With more than 10,000 works on display, the Museum galleries showcase glass selected from a permanent collection of more than 50,000 objects representing more than 3,500 years of history. The expansive collection is presented in three core galleries – 35 Centuries of Glass, Heineman, and Contemporary Art & Design – to tell the global story of glass from antiquity through the present day. The Innovation Galleries highlight scientific and technological achievements using glass, ranging from casserole dishes to telescopes to optical fiber.

CMoG is regarded as the conservation authority on glass to museums and institutions around the world.

In late 2024, the Museum celebrated the expansion of The Studio, funded primarily by a successful capital campaign. The Studio, which is celebrating its 30th anniversary in 2026, features the first large scale kiln casting facility in North America and can support over 100,000 Make Your Own Glass projects annually. The state-of-the-art facilities provide artists and students with the tools and the support they need to take risks and make discoveries; opportunities for people of all skill levels to forge and deepen their understanding of glass; and connections to the glass community, where artists gather to create, learn, and share.

Role Summary & Context For Recruitment

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) is responsible for the strategic planning, management, and success of the comprehensive fundraising efforts of the Corning Museum of Glass, including the pursuit of long-term relationships that benefit the financial health of the Museum. The CDO oversees policy, strategy, and execution of the work of the Development Department, which includes individual and planned giving, corporate, foundation and government giving, membership, giving appeals, special events, and donor relations programs. This leader reports to the Museum President and Executive Director, providing them with expert advice on all aspects of fundraising, including policy development and changes as well as new program directions. The CDO will manage all future campaigns. The CDO works closely with the Development Committee and Board of Trustees to build the Museum’s visibility, impact, and financial resources. The CDO serves as a champion for CMoG and the catalyst in strengthening the Museum’s culture of philanthropy.

The CDO oversees a team of seven staff members and provides strategic oversight and leadership for the Development Department’s annual operating budget.

Formal fundraising at CMoG is a relatively young discipline, having taken shape over the past decade alongside the Museum's landmark expansion of The Studio, and its successful capital campaign. As CMoG enters its next chapter, the Museum is investing in building a comprehensive, professionalized development program capable of matching the global stature of its collection, scholarship, and artistic community. The CDO will have the rare opportunity to help shape this program's strategy, systems, and team at an early and formative stage of its growth.

The CDO will be a close strategic partner and an active member of the Museum's leadership team. This is an opportunity to help shape CMoG's comprehensive strategic and fundraising plan, to be developed in partnership with the President and Board of Trustees over the coming year.

With a world-renowned glass collection, the preeminent Rakow Research Library, and a thriving community of working studio artists, CMoG offers an unusually rich philanthropic story. The CDO will have the opportunity to build Development’s presence among collector, scholarly, and design communities nationally and internationally, while deepening engagement with members and visitors closer to home.

Possesses a global orientation and knowledge of strategies and trends in global philanthropy.
Demonstrated supervisory and management skills, along with the ability to work effectively and professionally with people at all levels, including external stakeholders. Experience building or scaling a development department's infrastructure, systems, and team.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

Respects and exemplifies the mission, vision, and values of CMoG in all interactions with colleagues, staff, volunteers and the public.
Represents the Museum in a professional manner.
Adheres to all prescribed organizational and departmental policies and procedures.
Understands the Museum’s mission and programs; appreciates cultural environments; interested in the arts and museums.
Politically astute, diplomatic leader with excellent judgment who is able to navigate and align perspectives among donors, Board members, and staff.

Collaborative leader who builds and develops teams and shares credit for success.

We provide individuals with the tools they need to pursue their dreams and live meaningful lives. Department:
Landscape Architecture
Location:
Oakland, CA
Compensation:
$140,000 - $180,000 / year

Description

Alta is looking for a Landscape Architecture/Urban Design Business Development Director
to join our growing Oakland office design team. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who believes in the power of design and placemaking to create vibrant, active communities, and engaging public spaces.

In this role, you will drive business development and strategic growth throughout the Bay Area, Northern California, and the Pacific Northwest,
establishing Alta's presence and reputation with local city and regional government clients. You will be responsible for leading client relationship building, identifying new opportunities, and positioning Alta as a leader in sustainable landscape design and active transportation. This role requires a strategic thinker who can expand our market share while maintaining the high-quality, collaborative approach that defines our work.

You will also work on the design of projects with a focus on sustainability and active communities around the West and across the country. Design professionals who enjoy working closely with other disciplines will appreciate our Oakland team's multi-disciplinary approach that encourages collaboration with our planners, engineers, graphics designers, outreach specialists, and data analysts. If you are looking to join an innovative organization and do work that connects people to places while advancing social justice, safety, and environmental resilience, apply with Alta today!

About Alta

Alta is a mission‑driven company working to mitigate climate change and advance safety and social justice by shaping sustainable, people‑centered communities. We bring together expertise across planning, design, engineering, education and encouragement programs, and community engagement to help communities thrive. Our work is grounded in the belief that how places are designed and experienced has a profound impact on equity, health, and opportunity—and that people should always be at the heart of those decisions.

Founded in 1996, Alta was at the forefront of the active transportation movement and has spent nearly 30 years partnering with communities to imagine a more connected, resilient, and inclusive future. Today, with more than 225 staff across the United States and beyond, we are a global leader in creating environments that support everyday life, strengthen human connection, and respond to the challenges of a changing world. Alta offers the opportunity to collaborate across disciplines, contribute to meaningful work at every scale, and be part of a team committed to making lasting, positive change for people and the places they call home.

Day to Day

Day-to-day responsibilities for this role would include:
Leading business development efforts throughout Northern California and the Pacific Northwest including identifying opportunities, cultivating client relationships with local city and regional government agencies, and developing winning proposals and presentations.
Driving strategic market growth and positioning Alta as a leader in sustainable landscape architecture, urban design, and active transportation within the region.
Contributing to revenue growth targets for the Landscape Architecture business line in Northern California and the Pacific Northwest.
Building and maintaining relationships with key decision-makers at public agencies, participating in industry events, and representing Alta in the professional community.
Providing leadership and technical expertise to the Oakland and Portland Landscape Architecture design teams. In addition, collaborate with other disciplines (planning, engineering, data) as needed.
Mentoring design staff and contributing to internal professional development and training to design team.
Implementing best practices and process improvements to enhance project delivery efficiency and effectiveness.
Workload balancing for the Oakland and Portland Design teams.
Preparing schedules, budgets, and scope of services for projects.
Providing quality control over team deliverables.

Qualifications

Required

This position requires a combination of skills, experience and education including, but not limited to
15+ years of experience as a Landscape Architect or Urban Designer in a consulting environment or public entity
Bachelor's degree in Landscape Architecture or Urban Design
Professional Landscape Architect (PLA)
Experience in, or knowledge of corridors, such as greenways, trails, streets, or canals.
Demonstrated understanding of the design process and working collaboratively with other design disciplines and a detailed understanding of project management principles, methods and techniques.
Business acumen and demonstrated experience in business development and managing large contracts.
Ability to guide staff members and manage internal team expectations.
Exhibits strong initiative and ability to capitalize on opportunities to enhance Alta's position in the marketplace.
Ability to manage competing priorities, multiple simultaneous projects involving cross-functional project teams within budgetary and schedule constraints.
Excellent professional ethics, leadership skills, accountability, and decision-making capabilities.
Good presentation skills.
Proficiency in an enterprise-wide resource planning and project management tool.
Ability and willingness to travel.

Preferred

There are a number of additional skills, experience, and education that would be beneficial to this position including, but not limited to:
Experience managing large projects for both private and public clients.
Experience working in urban, rural, suburban, land use contexts.
Experience using Deltek Vision.
Active participation in industry-relevant professional associations and committees, such as ASLA or ULI.

What We Offer

Flexible Schedule

Alta offers a flexible, hybrid work schedule where most employees work from home three days per week. In-office days support our collaborative culture, one of our core values.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is $140,000-$180,000. This range reflects the company’s good faith estimate of the compensation for this position at the time of posting. Final compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location.

Benefits

Alta offers comprehensive benefits to all full-time employees:
Medical
: PPO or HSA medical plans, Alta pays 75% of the cost
Dental/Vision
: PPO, Alta pays 90% of the cost
Life Insurance
: Alta pays 100% of the premium for life and AD&D, equal to your base compensation
401(k)
: Alta provides a match up to 3%
PTO
: 21 days accrued annually to start
Holidays
: 11 total company paid holidays
Paid Parental Leave/Short-Term Disability

Additional Benefits
: Wellness reimbursement up to $800 annually, Alta Gets Around benefit of up to $900 annually, 5-year travel award, and professional development opportunities

: Ticketmaster

EVP, Head of Sports

Permanent, Full-Time, 40 hours per week

Who We Are

We’re fans who help fans everywhere get in to the live events they love. A proud division of Live Nation Entertainment, Ticketmaster has changed the way the world connects with their favorite artists, teams, and shows, and we continue to shape innovation every day. We’re not just selling tickets (though we do that better than anyone else), we’re enriching lives one amazing experience at a time. And we think that’s pretty amazing. If you’re passionate about the magic of live entertainment like we are, and you want to work at a company dedicated to helping millions of fans experience it, we want to hear from you.

THE TEAM

The Client Development team uses flexibility, creative thinking, organizational skills, and relationship building to work with our clients on our products, vision, and industry needs. This team of leaders, strategists and collaborators must always balance the unique best interests of our clients with Live Nation Entertainment’s vision and priorities. This team is client first and always ready to have the tough (and easy) conversations! We are part of the North American Client Development organization, working with Ticketmaster’s Global Marketplace organization, which sells over 500 million tickets each year across professional and college sports, theatre, arts, and concerts.

THE JOB

The Client Development Director (CDD) will focus exclusively on our client accounts, concentrating on the needs of clients within the TM Sports segment. This position will be responsible for managing, supporting and servicing the account related needs of any assigned set of clients in addition to sourcing and securing new business.

What You Will Be Doing

Operate as the voice of the customer internally by working with other Ticketmaster business leaders to provide incredible client experiences and outcomes
Direct and collaborate on the development of an account management blueprint, ensuring maximization of revenue and renewals within our client base.
Develop and implement strategies to upsell existing clients on products, programs, or services that drive ticket sales and revenue for your segment; track, monitor, and adjust plans to maximize results.
Develop, share, and implement best practices for assigned market segments.
Forecast clients’ tickets & revenue contribution to the segment’s annual business plan by developing client level business plans, including account strategy, profitability analysis, and program projections.
Complete ad hoc sales operations support as requested.
Monitor service levels provided by support teams to ensure SLA’s are being met.
Coach and collaborate with others on client support, marketing, and account management teams to ensure effective, consistent communication of Ticketmaster’s capabilities, services, and relevant offerings for our clients.
Responsible for retention of all clients within assigned portfolio, ensuring maximum margin levels through the renewal engagement.
Comprehensively collaborate with a cross-functional team, providing distinct support functions to clients, ultimately maximizing client satisfaction scores.
Identify new business opportunities, directing the client acquisition process against a set of annual sales goals.
Proactively conduct strategic account reviews with all assigned clients on a regular basis to review service needs and sales trends. Identify products and pricing that meet client needs and business objectives.
Development relationships with key system and product users providing product team with client feedback on product enhancements.
Assist in the identification of opportunities for new products and enhancements for development of existing products.
Address client concerns and ensure for the resolution of issues in a timely manner, with follow-up when appropriate.
Deliver ongoing market analysis and assessment of competitors and market intelligence with a focus on the future and value creation.
Maintain company’s contact management database (Salesforce) with accurate, up-to-date contact and account details.

Organization Overview

Founded in 1951 by Corning Incorporated as a gift to the nation, the Corning Museum of Glass (CMoG) is the global center for the art, science, and history of glass.

The Museum shapes the understanding and appreciation of glass worldwide and draws more than 300,000 visitors each year to a city of roughly 10,000 residents. The New York Times named CMoG as one of the U.S. museums to see in 2025, and Newsweek readers voted CMoG one of the Top 3 Best Art Museums in America.

With more than 10,000 works on display, the Museum galleries showcase glass selected from a permanent collection of more than 50,000 objects representing more than 3,500 years of history. The expansive collection is presented in three core galleries – 35 Centuries of Glass, Heineman, and Contemporary Art & Design – to tell the global story of glass from antiquity through the present day. The Innovation Galleries highlight scientific and technological achievements using glass, ranging from casserole dishes to telescopes to optical fiber.

CMoG is regarded as the conservation authority on glass to museums and institutions around the world.

In late 2024, the Museum celebrated the expansion of The Studio, funded primarily by a successful capital campaign. The Studio, which is celebrating its 30th anniversary in 2026, features the first large scale kiln casting facility in North America and can support over 100,000 Make Your Own Glass projects annually. The state-of-the-art facilities provide artists and students with the tools and the support they need to take risks and make discoveries; opportunities for people of all skill levels to forge and deepen their understanding of glass; and connections to the glass community, where artists gather to create, learn, and share.

Role Summary & Context For Recruitment

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) is responsible for the strategic planning, management, and success of the comprehensive fundraising efforts of the Corning Museum of Glass, including the pursuit of long-term relationships that benefit the financial health of the Museum. The CDO oversees policy, strategy, and execution of the work of the Development Department, which includes individual and planned giving, corporate, foundation and government giving, membership, giving appeals, special events, and donor relations programs. This leader reports to the Museum President and Executive Director, providing them with expert advice on all aspects of fundraising, including policy development and changes as well as new program directions. The CDO will manage all future campaigns. The CDO works closely with the Development Committee and Board of Trustees to build the Museum’s visibility, impact, and financial resources. The CDO serves as a champion for CMoG and the catalyst in strengthening the Museum’s culture of philanthropy.

The CDO oversees a team of seven staff members and provides strategic oversight and leadership for the Development Department’s annual operating budget.

Formal fundraising at CMoG is a relatively young discipline, having taken shape over the past decade alongside the Museum's landmark expansion of The Studio, and its successful capital campaign. As CMoG enters its next chapter, the Museum is investing in building a comprehensive, professionalized development program capable of matching the global stature of its collection, scholarship, and artistic community. The CDO will have the rare opportunity to help shape this program's strategy, systems, and team at an early and formative stage of its growth.

The CDO will be a close strategic partner and an active member of the Museum's leadership team. This is an opportunity to help shape CMoG's comprehensive strategic and fundraising plan, to be developed in partnership with the President and Board of Trustees over the coming year.

With a world-renowned glass collection, the preeminent Rakow Research Library, and a thriving community of working studio artists, CMoG offers an unusually rich philanthropic story. The CDO will have the opportunity to build Development’s presence among collector, scholarly, and design communities nationally and internationally, while deepening engagement with members and visitors closer to home.

Position Summary:

The position (K0239384)

Position Summary & Responsibilities:

Directs and oversees the operations of the Solid Waste Permits Section to ensure that program staff apply regulations and BWM policies correctly, and ensure work is completed and reviewed by appropriate staff by monitoring the monthly metrics reports and tracking project timelines. Work of the section includes (1) Managing permitted activity for active solid waste facilities including landfilling, groundwater monitoring at landfills, composting, solid waste processing, and transfer station operation; (2) Reviewing applications for new permits and permit modifications of solid waste landfills; (3) Reviewing applications for approvable activities such as special wase disposal, composting, land application, disposal without a permit, and landfarming; (4) Reviewing environmental sampling reports for landfill gas and groundwater monitoring; and (4) Reviewing closure and post-closure cost estimates for permitted facilities to ensure adequate financial assurance. Work includes setting performance goals, supporting staff development, training new staff, providing technical guidance to staff, communicating expectations to all section staff, and stimulating productivity.

Job Responsibilities may include but are not limited to the following:

Directly supervise the Solid Waste Landfills Unit Chief, Solid Waste Hydrogeology Unit Chief, Solid Waste Processing Unit Chief, and the Chanute office engineer. Use the Kansas Learning and Performance Management System to establish annual performance objectives and document at least mid-year feedback sessions and annual performance evaluations. Apply personnel policies consistently and equitably to staff. Establish track performance metrics and work with Unit Chiefs to resolve deficiencies in program performance. Review and approve Section work products as appropriate including correspondence, permits, and approvals. Promote teamwork and a positive work environment.
